statusDetail: Coverage complete: 58/58 checks judged across six representative public paths and one failure state.

page.notes: Arabic adult-media catalog. Public catalog, search, category, album, video detail, sign-in and 404 surfaces were sampled.

checkOutcomes.method: Default/dark screenshot comparison plus CSS/computed-style probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark-emulation screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture; computed color-scheme is normal and no prefers-color-scheme CSS was found. The dark UI is hard-coded rather than preference-driven.
The reduced-motion probe matched the requested preference, found no running animations and no auto-advancing content.
Forced-colors/prefers-contrast capture retained visible text, controls, boundaries and selected-state cues.

checkOutcomes.method: Cross-path visual walkthrough plus CSS feature probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Navigation between the long listing, category, search and detail pages is an abrupt full-document swap; no authored view-transition CSS was present.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature probe, scroll walkthrough and trace summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked visual effects or scroll-event-driven animation were observed; scrolling remains native and the trace shows only one 56.65 ms task.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile walkthrough and player DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The feed and player use native scrolling and native media controls; no custom pointer-drag behavior that fights platform gestures was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Long-page layout plus mobile screenshot and CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage is about 13,943 CSS px tall at mobile width, but screenshots and CSS probe show static chrome with no progress, back-to-top, shrinking header or scroll-state behavior.
No edge-attached tooltip or popover surface was found that requires anchored positioning; the sign-in surface is a centered modal.
Prominent section headings, selected sort state and card hierarchy consistently direct attention across listing and search views.
Lighthouse observed a third-party push SDK requesting notification permission on page load, interrupting users before an in-context action.

checkOutcomes.method: Active overlay interaction and semantic DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Opening sign-in creates .fancybox-overlay/.fancybox-wrap divs; the page contains zero dialog and zero popover elements, and focus remained on body rather than moving into the modal.
The first viewport gives most space to search and media cards; decoration and borders are restrained relative to content.
At 360x800, homepage and video detail both report scrollWidth 360, viewport meta present and 0 px horizontal overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed CSS and mobile/desktop component comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Cards reflow at viewport breakpoints, but computed container-type is normal and the stylesheet probe found no @container rules, so reusable components are viewport-coupled.
The first focusable sign-up control computes outline:none and box-shadow:none; two category links are only 15 px high, below an adequate touch target.
The Arabic tagline, search field, category shortcuts and media cards make the site purpose and next actions immediately apparent.
A search for arab returns 12 video links, and a selected canonical detail URL reaches a working video player with controls.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP status request and rendered error-state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A nonexistent route returns HTTP 404, displays an explicit Arabic not-found message, and retains search and related-content recovery routes.
Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 7.6 s and TTI 7.6 s despite CLS 0 and TBT 70 ms; the LCP is well outside the good threshold.
Both mobile layout captures report CLS 0 with no shifts, and all 44 homepage images have explicit dimensions.
The trace found one 56.65 ms long task and only 6.65 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 70 ms.

checkOutcomes.method: Image audit, HAR summary and DOM script attributes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page loads 41 below-fold images eagerly; all 44 images lack srcset, and the HAR identifies two render-blocking stylesheets plus an undeferred parser script.
Lighthouse estimates 262 KiB unused JavaScript and 20 KiB unused CSS; main.min.js is 69% unused and the stylesheet is 84% unused.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audit and control-name probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found the linked logo has no discernible name; the menu button also lacks an accessible name in the DOM probe.
Lighthouse measured 2.26:1 on the active pagination state and 1.79:1 on footer text/links, below WCAG minimums.
Programmatically focusing the first control produces outline:none and no box shadow; opening sign-in leaves focus on body rather than in the modal.
Primary card titles and headings are readable at mobile width without clipping; Arabic text wraps within cards and viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: Video track probe plus target-size and mobile reflow checks
checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative detail page exposes two video elements but neither contains a caption/subtitle track; the target probe also found two 15 px-high category links.
Lighthouse recorded no browser console errors or uncaught exceptions during load.
The document has an HTML doctype, UTF-8 charset and viewport meta; all 44 audited images have dimensions and none is oversized beyond 2x display width.
Lighthouse found a notification request on load and three BFCache failure reasons caused by Cache-Control:no-store/cookie modification.
The homepage and representative video have descriptive titles and meta descriptions.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability primitive, robots recon and Lighthouse anchor audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw content coverage is 100% and robots is valid, but Lighthouse found sign-in and five AJAX sort anchors without href, making those actions uncrawlable and non-progressive.
Homepage and detail canonical URLs are present, robots permits public content, sitemap indexes current content, and tested pages return appropriate 200/404 statuses.
The video detail supplies Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD VideoObject, while the homepage has neither Open Graph tags nor JSON-LD.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent; all five cookies lack Secure, use SameSite=None, and PHPSESSID is not HttpOnly.
The tracker probe found seven third-party origins and active Google Tag Manager/Analytics; the HAR attributes 50 of 54 requests and 813,138 transferred bytes to third parties.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission audit and sign-in DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports notification permission requested on load, while the public sign-in page offers password-only authentication and no WebAuthn/passkey surface.
CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all absent.
The discoverability primitive found 100% raw/rendered content coverage, no empty SPA mount and useful crawler rendering without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: Cross-path walkthrough and Lighthouse console audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative listing, search and detail routes render complete content without console errors; the native player and server navigation remain usable.
This is a server-rendered streaming/catalog site whose core media is intrinsically network-dependent; installability and offline media playback are not a proportionate requirement.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a server-rendered streaming/catalog site whose core media is intrinsically network-dependent; installability and offline media playback are not a proportionate requirement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A missing route returns a real 404, explains that the page moved or is unavailable, and retains search plus related links for recovery.
The Arabic-first RTL interface declares html lang="en" and no dir attribute, giving assistive technology and bidi layout the wrong language/direction signals.
Rendered dates and counts use Arabic labels and relative-age wording consistently across listing and detail templates.
The audited public surfaces show relative ages and durations only; they do not schedule or coordinate time-zone-sensitive events.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public surfaces show relative ages and durations only; they do not schedule or coordinate time-zone-sensitive events.

checkOutcomes.method: Search flow text probe and first-viewport screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: The search page places a block of unrelated external keyword-stuffed links above the genuine results, including arbadasex.com and hot-arab-films URLs, obscuring the result set and resembling disguised SEO content.

checkOutcomes.method: Sign-in form DOM and screenshot inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The sign-in form has visible Arabic labels and prominent account creation and password/email recovery links; the public search requires no validation-sensitive data.
Sign-in username and password inputs have empty autocomplete values instead of username and current-password; the search field also has no autocomplete token.
The public sign-in surface clearly labels credentials and exposes free registration plus password/email recovery; no purchase, subscription or forced-continuity flow is present on audited paths.
All 44 homepage images are legacy JPG, none has srcset, and 41 below-fold images load eagerly.

checkOutcomes.method: Trace, memory metrics and player probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CDP trace reports only 6.65 ms total blocking time and the repeated-scroll probe adds no DOM nodes; no persistent autoplay media was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary, tracker and image audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: Third parties account for 813,138 of 826,210 transferred bytes (98.4%); Google Tag Manager alone transfers 166,718 bytes and 41 below-fold images load eagerly.
No developer intent indicates an agent-facing transaction surface; this public media catalog can be crawled fully without JavaScript, so WebMCP exposure is an optional emerging opportunity.
checkOutcomes.reason: No developer intent indicates an agent-facing transaction surface; this public media catalog can be crawled fully without JavaScript, so WebMCP exposure is an optional emerging opportunity.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative search and media-browsing tasks do not require on-device generative inference; absence is not a quality failure for this site.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative search and media-browsing tasks do not require on-device generative inference; absence is not a quality failure for this site.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap comparison and same-session metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-page down/up scroll cycles, heap summary size rose only 59,903 bytes (8,554,048 to 8,613,951), DOM element count remained 867, and no unbounded trend was demonstrated.
The loaded media listing retained about 8.6 MB of heap-summary self size with 867 live DOM elements, proportionate to a 44-card image catalog.

checkOutcomes.method: Before/after heap summary and DOM-count comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Repeated scrolling added zero DOM elements; detached-node constructors do not appear among the heap summaries’ largest constructors, and the post snapshot changed by only about 60 KB.

principleOutcomes.reason: No developer intent indicates an agent-facing transaction surface; this public media catalog can be crawled fully without JavaScript, so WebMCP exposure is an optional emerging opportunity. The representative search and media-browsing tasks do not require on-device generative inference; absence is not a quality failure for this site.

paths.description: Homepage and primary media listing: purpose, navigation, preferences, performance, responsive layout and global policies.
Arabic category listing, representing taxonomy/listing templates.
Search journey for “arab”, representing query results and content discovery.
Canonical video detail and player, representing the core media-consumption journey.
Public sign-in entry, representing account form semantics and recovery.
Nonexistent route, representing HTTP and user-facing recovery.

findings.summary: Hard-coded dark palette ignores the user theme preference
findings.evidence: The default and dark-emulation captures are pixel-identical; color-scheme computes to normal and no theme media query exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() so browser UI and site surfaces follow the user preference.

findings.summary: Route changes have no continuity cue
findings.evidence: Representative MPA route changes are abrupt and no view-transition CSS is authored.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same- or cross-document View Transitions for list-to-detail navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Very long listings provide no scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage is 13,943 CSS px tall but has no progress, back-to-top, shrinking header or scroll-state affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress/back-to-top affordance using scroll-state queries or a scroll-position-aware element.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested on load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse notification-on-start failed and identifies js.wpshsdk.com push code as the source.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the on-load request and ask only after a clear user action that explains the benefit.

findings.summary: Sign-in uses a custom, focus-unsafe overlay
findings.evidence: The interaction creates Fancybox divs, no dialog/popover exists, and focus remains on body.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with a labelled heading, initial focus, Escape/light-dismiss policy and restored trigger focus.

findings.summary: Cards are viewport-coupled rather than container-responsive
findings.evidence: No @container rule exists and container-type computes to normal despite cards appearing in multiple layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/list wrappers container-type and move component breakpoints to @container rules.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch targets are inadequate
findings.evidence: The first focused control has no outline or box shadow; category links are 15 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and enlarge compact controls to at least a comfortable 24x24 CSS px minimum, preferably 44x44.

findings.summary: Largest content paint is slow on mobile
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP and TTI at 7.6 seconds; trace warm conditions were faster, so the throttled mobile result exposes the risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP thumbnail, lazy-load below-fold cards, reduce blocking resources and remeasure under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Below-fold images and parser resources load inefficiently
findings.evidence: 41 below-fold images are eager, all 44 lack srcset, and the HAR shows blocking CSS and a parser-inserted undeferred main script.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images, add responsive sources, prioritise only the LCP image and defer noncritical scripts/styles.

findings.summary: Most shipped JavaScript and CSS is unused
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 262 KiB unused JS and 20 KiB unused CSS, including 69% of main.min.js and 84% of the primary stylesheet.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific bundles, remove dead rules and load push/analytics code only after consent or intent.

findings.summary: Logo and menu controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags the linked logo and the DOM probe shows an unlabeled icon-only menu button.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise accessible names and retain semantic button/link roles for every interactive control.

findings.summary: Pagination and footer text fail contrast minimums
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 2.26:1 for active pagination and 1.79:1 for footer text and links.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose foreground/background pairs meeting at least 4.5:1 for normal text and verify all states.

findings.summary: Focus is invisible and not moved into the modal
findings.evidence: Focused controls show no indicator and opening sign-in leaves activeElement on body.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement visible :focus-visible styles and native dialog focus management with trigger restoration.

findings.summary: Video content has no caption track
findings.evidence: Both video elements on the representative detail page contain zero track elements and no subtitle/caption surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide WebVTT captions and a transcript or equivalent for spoken content, with a visible caption control.

findings.summary: Push prompting and no-store policies harm platform behavior
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds an on-load notification request and three BFCache blockers tied to no-store/cookie modification.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsolicited push code and scope no-store only to genuinely sensitive responses so public catalog pages can use BFCache.

findings.summary: Important actions are not real links
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds sign-in and five AJAX sorting anchors without href even though raw content otherwise has 100% crawler coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every navigable action a real href and progressively enhance sorting/modal behavior with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Rich media metadata is incomplete
findings.evidence: The detail page has Open Graph tags but no VideoObject JSON-LD; the homepage has no OG or JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject and Organization/WebSite JSON-LD plus complete social preview metadata.

findings.summary: Session cookies and transport defenses are unsafe
findings.evidence: CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent; every cookie lacks Secure and uses SameSite=None, while PHPSESSID lacks HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly and appropriate SameSite attributes, then deploy HSTS, nosniff and a tested CSP.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party traffic dominate the load
findings.evidence: Seven third-party origins are active; 50 of 54 requests and 813,138 bytes are third-party, including Google analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit necessity, delay analytics until consent, batch events and self-host or remove nonessential dependencies.

findings.summary: Permissions are not contextual and authentication is password-only
findings.evidence: A push SDK requests notification permission on load; sign-in offers username/password with no passkey path.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate notification requests behind explicit intent and add WebAuthn/passkey registration and authentication where accounts matter.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out a report-only CSP first, then enforce CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Arabic pages declare English language and no direction
findings.evidence: The Arabic-first homepage has html lang="en" and no dir attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="ar" and dir="rtl" at the document root, then use logical CSS properties and override language on embedded non-Arabic fragments.

findings.summary: Search results are preceded by disguised keyword links
findings.evidence: The arab search displays unrelated external URLs and keyword-stuffed text above the actual result heading and cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove injected/SEO link blocks and show only clearly labelled, relevant search results or sponsored content with provenance.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autofill semantics
findings.evidence: Username and password inputs have empty autocomplete values; the search input is also unspecified.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and "current-password" on sign-in, plus appropriate search semantics.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and device resources
findings.evidence: All 44 audited images are JPG, none has srcset, and 41 below-fold images load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes, preserve dimensions and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Third-party and eager-media cost is disproportionate
findings.evidence: Third parties are 98.4% of transferred bytes and 41 below-fold thumbnails load without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party/media budget, remove or defer push/analytics, and lazy-load responsive thumbnails.

taskList.title: Secure cookies, headers and defensive browser policies
Remove on-load push permission and gate tracking behind intent
Fix mobile LCP and image/resource loading
Restore accessible names, contrast, focus and captions
Remove disguised keyword links from search
Replace Fancybox sign-in with a semantic dialog
Correct Arabic language and direction metadata
Make links crawlable and add structured media metadata
Add sign-in autocomplete and passkey support
Adopt preference-driven theming and modern navigation cues
Move reusable card adaptation to container queries
